cards.title: How a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light
prereqs: light travels in straight lines from a source
transparent and translucent materials let some light through
cards.opens_by: Recall that opaque materials block light while transparent and translucent materials let some through, so the learner is ready to ask what happens to the light that gets blocked.
cards.objective: Explain why a shadow appears when an opaque object blocks light, and describe the position of the shadow relative to the light source

misconceptions.description: A shadow is a thing the object gives off or sends out, so it appears wherever the object is, regardless of where the light is.
The shadow forms on the same side of the object as the light source, or on the object's lit side, because that is the side the light touches.
Any object at all produces a full shadow, so transparent things like a glass window also cast a solid dark shadow like a wall does.

prior_knowledge: Light comes from a source and travels in straight lines
Light sources emit light; objects that do not emit light are seen by reflected light
Examples of light sources include the Sun, lamps, torches
Opaque materials block all light and form shadows
Transparent materials allow most light to pass through and form little or no shadow
Translucent materials allow some light to pass through and form a faint shadow
